Conclusion In this paper, mitigation of E2 and E3 disturbances was addressed. A 4-leg inverter was utilized for the output portion of an SST. Additionally, a nonlinearHamiltoniancontrolwasproposedtomitigatetheDCvoltageoffset induced by the CM voltage. The Hamiltonian control was designed to serve 2 purposes: enforce Lyapunov stability; track current setpoints. Mathematical analysiswasusedtoestablishthattheproposedHamiltoniancontrollerwould satisfy both of these criteria. For all cases examined, the proposed controller was successful in both stabilizing the system and driving the currents to the desired setpoints. Additionally, the proposed control scheme was able to protect the inverter switches from excessive and potentially damaging overvoltage stress. Also, hardware results were presented. The hardware results showed that when a potentially damaging common mode voltage step occurs, the con- troller is able to rapidly recover the current waveform. This was established for the prolonged E3-type insult. However, the hardware needs further de- veloped to mitigate faster E2-type insults. This progress in ongoing and will be presented in future work. Additionally, in future work, the full SST will be examined. The ability of the controller to mitigate CM voltage impact is limited by the magnitude of the input voltage to the output inverter. Additionally, a DAB control will be investigated to compensate for larger CM voltage injections. 8.
